sentences.text: Yunganglong possessed a skull that was relatively wide and low.

The caudal surface of the supraoccipital bone in Yunganglong is inclined steeply forward at approximately 45 degrees, distinguishing it from more primitive relatives, such as early hadrosauroids, where it is nearly vertical.
The genus name honors the Yungang Grottoes, a UNESCO World Heritage site located about 50 km from the fossil discovery site, and includes the Chinese word for 'dragon'.
The species name refers to the city of Datong in northern Shanxi Province, where the holotype specimen was discovered.
Yunganglong was first described and named by a team of eight researchers led by Run-Fu Wang in 2013.
The fossils were collected in 2011 as part of a project initiated by the Department of Land and Resources of Shanxi Province to supply the Shanxi Museum of Geology.
Remains were gathered from locality 7 of the Zhumapu Formation.
The dinosaur is known only from a single disarticulated partial skeleton, holotype SXMG V 00001, which is housed at the Shanxi Museum of Geology.
In addition to the Yunganglong holotype, ankylosaur and ceratopsian fossils were found at the same localities.
Yunganglong was a ground-dwelling herbivore capable of both bipedal and quadrupedal locomotion.
The genus Yunganglong contains only one known species, Yunganglong datongensis.
Yunganglong is classified within the superfamily Hadrosauroidea.
Yunganglong belongs to the infraorder Iguanodontia.
Phylogenetic analysis places Yunganglong as more advanced than Probactrosaurus, within an unresolved group with other early hadrosauroids like Jintasaurus and Protohadros.
Strict consensus analysis places Yunganglong as more derived than Probactrosaurus, within an unresolved polytomy with several other basal hadrosauriforms and the Aralosaurus-Hadrosauridae clade.
The animal is classified within the class Ornithischia.
Fossils of Yunganglong were found in the lower Zhumapu Formation in Zuoyun County, Shanxi Province, in northeastern China.
Yunganglong lived during the mid-Cretaceous period, approximately 100 to 95 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage.
Yunganglong lived between the Cenomanian and Santonian stages, approximately 100.5 to 83.6 million years ago.
The first dinosaur record for Shanxi province was reported by Young in 1958 from two localities in Zuoyun County.
